## Design system (ds-workflow 0.2.0)

This project's UI comes only from the design system **小浣熊教育版设计系统** — source: Figma file `lmbRXNuIp0ZsJ4LI32T2ZK`, starting at node 290:16856; pinned version in `design-system/lock.json`. Proposals and written-back screens go to Figma file `lmbRXNuIp0ZsJ4LI32T2ZK`. Before writing pages, components or styles, or doing any Figma task, read `docs/ds-workflow/README.md`, then the playbook for the task.

**Hard rules**
1. **Visual values are tokens only.** Colours, font sizes, font weights, spacing, radii and shadows are written as `var(--xhx-*)`, generated by `npx ds-workflow build` into `src/styles/xhx-tokens.css`. Never edit that file by hand and never write colour literals or font names. If the design system lacks a value, propose it in `design-system/tokens/proposed.tokens.json` (`playbooks/ds-propose`) instead of hard-coding it.
2. **The component library (`src/ui`) uses tokens only, no px.** One Figma component set = one code component; its variant properties are the props. Pages only compose components and lay them out.
3. **Reuse, then extend, then create.** For every UI element, first look for a design-system component, then add a variant to an existing one, and only then create `Proposed/<Area>/<Name>`. Record the result in `design-system/components.registry.json` with status reuse / extend / proposed / approved / deprecated.
4. **Write back to Figma with component instances only.** Build frames with the Figma MCP `use_figma`; never HTML-to-design imports or screenshots. Proposals go on the "Proposed" page, screens on the "Screens · {label}" page. If your agent cannot write to Figma, hand the write-back to someone who can (`ds-review-loop`); do not substitute anything else.
5. **Every UI change goes to the designer for review, automatically, and finished screens are never overwritten** (`ds-review-loop`). Sections whose name starts with "✅ Ready" and everything in `design-system/figma-review.json` under `ready` / `unconfirmed` are the designer's: put changes in a v2 beside them, and only add variants to components they use. Remind the designer through the channel the project chose (figma), mark changed frames "· 🟡 In review", and record the batch under `pending`. When a section becomes Ready, align the code to it (`ds-align-ready-for-dev`).
6. **`npx ds-workflow check` must pass before every commit.** If it fails, fix the code. Never update the baseline to pass (`--update` is only for after a migration), never delete checks.
7. **Everything is pinned to a version.** Upgrade the design system through `ds-upgrade`: sync, diff report, migrate, verify. Never edit only the token file.
8. **Shared state lives in the repo, not in an agent.** Pinned version, registry, review ledger and proposals are files in the repo, so every agent and every person sees the same state. Never keep it only in an agent's memory or a chat, and update the files in the same change as the code.
9. **Only people decide.** An agent never marks a proposal approved, a section Ready, or a review done (it only records in the repo what a person decided), and never releases to production while `npx ds-workflow review --strict` fails.

**Commands**: `npx ds-workflow sync …` (sync and pin) · `build` (token CSS) · `check` (gate) · `registry` (render the registry `docs/design/component-registry.md`) · `review` (the review ledger; `--strict` before a production release) · `rules` (refresh this block and the playbook copies)

**Playbooks** (`docs/ds-workflow/`)
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-adopt/SKILL.md` — Use when a project adopts a design system for the first time (a Figma file or a link into one, a Figma Community kit, the team's published library, or the designer's HTML export), or to fill in a missing design-system/ directory - initializes ds-workflow, records the source, syncs and pins a version, generates token CSS, turns on the check, and builds a legacy alias layer for existing styles.
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-align-ready-for-dev/SKILL.md` — Use when the designer has changed screens in Figma and marked sections Ready for dev - reads the screens and new components in those sections, compares them item by item with the current code, updates the code to match the design, verifies with screenshots, and updates token proposals and the registry.
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-implement/SKILL.md` — Use for any change to UI code - styles, components or pages (stages 5, 7) - so that the component library uses only design system tokens, props map one-to-one to Figma variants and pages only compose components, then run the check, e2e tests and visual regression.
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-map/SKILL.md` — Use before writing UI for a new screen or feature area, or when auditing an existing UI (stage 2) - maps every element of every UI state to a design system component + variant or token, fills in the component registry, and lists missing variants, components and tokens.
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-propose/SKILL.md` — Use when the design system lacks a component, variant or token (stages 3–4) - builds marked component sets, extension copies and proposed variables on the Figma proposal page with the Figma MCP use_figma, asks the designer for review through the project's review channel and waits, instead of hard-coding the missing value in code.
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-review-loop/SKILL.md` — Use whenever new or changed UI goes to Figma for the designer to review - runs automatically after any UI change (new screen, new state, changed layout, interaction or copy position, new variant), reads which sections the designer marked Ready, never overwrites them (adds a v2 beside them), reminds the designer where they work, and records everything in the review ledger.
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-upgrade/SKILL.md` — Use when the design system publishes a new version, a proposal is approved and merged into the library, or the designer creates new library styles or components, and before starting a new feature area - re-syncs, reads the generated diff report, migrates code and the registry, runs the check and visual regression, and updates the pinned version.
- `docs/ds-workflow/ds-write-back/SKILL.md` — Use to write UI states back to Figma as components (stage 6) - builds each screen from design system and proposal component instances with the Figma MCP use_figma and places them on the Screens page for the designer, without touching screens the designer marked Ready; never use HTML-to-design imports or full-screen screenshots.
